title: Endurance mode: issues found in testing
acceptance: The issues the user found in Endurance mode are written down, reproduced and fixed; a full Endurance game plays correctly
notes: Added 2026-11-12. Issues found: (1) with Autoplay on, the first two arrows of every new lap are missed; (2) after pausing at lap 4 and changing settings, the camera stutters on unpause, jumping forward every few seconds. Cause (from the log): Endurance plays the music faster each lap, and the smooth song clock went back to the normal tempo whenever it re-synced (after a pause, at a lap loop). Running too slowly it fell behind, re-synced with a jump, and the re-sync also restarted the tempo measurement, so at high lap tempos it never recovered. The jumps skipped past the first arrows of a lap (Autoplay presses within 50 ms) and moved the camera in steps. Fix in src/song_clock.cpp: a re-sync keeps the measured tempo (only a new song, at its Get Ready screen, starts from normal), and an ordinary correction no longer restarts the measurement; the tempo is logged as [songclock] tempo now N.NNx. To test: Endurance with Autoplay to lap 4 or later, a pause with settings changes; no missed lap-start arrows and no camera stutter. 2026-11-12, test of the song clock fix: Autoplay still misses the first few notes of each lap. Parked by the user as a known bug, to be fixed after release (moved to the post-release list). Also to check: hit timing (Input Offset advice) ignores presses when the song runs over 10% fast, so later Endurance laps give no timing data.

title: Game volume boost
acceptance: BBRR Settings > Game Volume 100-200%; loud passages rounded off by a limiter instead of distorting; a log line reports how loud the game mix is
notes: Requested 2026-11-12: the game is quieter than other programs at full volume. The SDK already had an output gain (rex/audio/downmix.h) that nothing set; it hard-clipped above full scale. SDK patch 0018 applies a gain above 1 after the channel mix with a soft limiter (knee at 0.8) and logs every 30 s the game mix peak and average level and how much was rounded off. Setting --game_volume, default 100%. Built, not run; the level line will show how much headroom the game leaves. Measured 2026-11-12 at 100% (Denon AVR, 6 channels): during songs the game mix peaks at -2 to 0 dBFS (bursts) but averages only -27 to -34 dBFS across the six channels (about -22 to -29 dBFS on the two front channels that carry the music), roughly 10 dB below typical PC audio. A wide-dynamic-range mix: a plain boost reaches the limiter on loud bursts. Suggested: try 150%-175% and watch the 'rounded off' share in the log; a compressor (lifting the quiet parts) would be the better long-term fix. Tested at 150% 2026-11-12: output peaks reach full scale only on bursts and 0.002-0.014% of samples were rounded off (inaudible); room to go higher. Settled 2026-11-12: no menu setting; the game plays at 150% by default (--game_volume to change it). Done.

title: Improved city lighting
acceptance: Firework light reflected on city (dynamic point lights), optional
notes: Researched 2026-11-11 (docs/GRAPHICS.md): city is texture x one scene-wide ambient colour, no normals; plan = per-firework light list + replaced city shader. Ray tracing only as a later hybrid (shadows/reflections); RTX Remix not applicable. 2026-11-12: started on branch city-lighting (tag pre-city-lighting marks the version before it; that build's exe and DLLs are copied to out/backup-pre-city-lighting). Chosen route: per-building tint - each city draw gets its own ambient colour from nearby fireworks - instead of per-pixel lighting, which needs shader replacement (R-408). Step 1, built, not run: a probe (--city_light_probe, src/city_lighting.cpp, SDK patch 0009) that logs every draw of one frame 12 s and 25 s into a song (shader constants, vertex box), the first firework bursts and spark emitters. Nothing on screen changes yet. Probe results 2026-11-12 (two runs): the city's pixel shaders (238C, C9D2, 88B6) already light per pixel from one point light - position c15, colour c16, strength c17.x, inverse-square falloff - while the game keeps six firework lights and gives them all only to the smoke shader (vertex shader BBFF: positions c8-c13, colour and strength c16-c21). City pieces are world-space draws, about 1,000 small ones plus a few hundred chunks. Step 2, built, not run: SDK patch 0011 gives every city draw its own stand-in light for all six fireworks as seen from that piece; setting City Lighting (Off / Low / Medium / High / Very High = strength 1, 2, 4, 8; --city_lighting) in Video Settings, off by default. '[bbrr] city light' log lines show the game's own values next to ours. Also learned: the main picture is drawn without multisampling (for R-405). First test 2026-11-12: works and looks better than the original (colours more pronounced, the flash spreads over buildings more naturally); Low almost imperceptible, Very High quite strong; seams between pieces; rooftops not bright enough. The log showed the first version's brightness followed the game's own flash (c17.x starts at 500,000 and dies within frames) instead of the lights' own strengths. Second version (SDK patch 0012), built, not run: fixed brightness scale (strength 1 = the game's flash at its peak, lasting as long as the game's smoke lights do); every piece lit from one shared centre so the falloff is continuous (large pieces get the total colour, small ones the mix arriving at them); flat faces brighter when facing the light (the shader ignores surface direction for this light); the game's own flash kept on top; new top level Extreme (32). Second version confirmed in play 2026-11-12 with screenshots: 'looks great', significantly improved; Medium and High look best. The top level is over the top but kept at the user's request, renamed Acid Trip. Still on branch city-lighting, not merged to main. Later the same day: a brightness ceiling was added (patches 0013-0016) because walls near a burst or a rising rocket washed out to white: the light is kept at least 350 units from each piece's box and the piece's nearest point gets no more than the ceiling; light colours get a share of white so textures still show. The user tried ceilings in play and chose 0.35 (0.5 and above blow out; small patches of strong colour remain at 0.35, accepted for now - probably wide blocks, which cannot be bounded this way). Measured cost on the user's PC: 0.10-0.15 ms a frame. Default is now Medium, ceiling 0.35 (--city_light_ceiling). scripts/build.ps1 now copies the SDK's DLLs every time (an SDK-only change was not reaching the game). Marked done and merged into main 2026-11-12 at the user's request. Possible follow-up, not planned: a rough 3D map of the city so the ceiling also holds on wide blocks.

notes: Researched 2026-11-12 (docs/GRAPHICS.md, Water reflections): the water samples a mirror pass of the sky, city and ground-level lights; the sparks and smoke are only drawn in the normal pass. Correction to the research: the 4,000-point draw 63B4/4B1E is not the sparks (its pixel shader multiplies by c11.x = 0, so it draws nothing: likely a star field switched off); the bursts are BA59/7C30 (up to ~19,000 points), the lit smoke BBFF/9567, and rockets with their trails 1DB9/C471 are already in the mirror pass. Water Glow (--water_glow): the water's single specular highlight (light position c2, shininess c3, colour c4; the moon) is moved to this frame's fireworks and given their colour, shininess 20. Water Reflections (--water_reflections): the burst draw is issued a second time with the mirror camera captured from the city's mirror pass (C837 c0-c3); whether it shows depends on whether the water writes depth - the first frame logs the depth state of the water and burst draws ('[bbrr] water draw: depth test ...'). SDK patch 0019. Test 2026-11-12: Water Glow looked really nice and is to be kept (now on by default at Medium) - but only the rocket tails showed in the water, and the user wants the light that falls on the buildings to fall on the water too. Patch 0020: the highlight spreads wider (shininess 6 instead of 20; Video Settings > Water Glow Spread: Narrow 20 / Medium 6 / Wide 2) and the fireworks' colour washes over the water (ambient green and blue, --water_glow_wash 0.06; red is left alone as it also sets the water's opacity). Water Glow has levels Off / Low / Medium / High. Water Reflections: the log shows the burst draw has no depth test (and the water writes depth), so the mirrored copy painted over everything - seen in visualizer mode. Doing it properly means drawing the bursts into the mirror picture before the water reads it (a register-state snapshot replayed in the next frame's mirror pass); kept as 'Water Reflections (test)', off by default. Settled 2026-11-12: the Spread row is gone, the highlight is always Narrow (shininess 20; --water_glow_spread still works); Water Glow Off / Low / Medium / High with High the default. 2026-11-12: the Water Reflections (test) option was taken out of the menu and the reflections are forced off in code (src/city_lighting.cpp); post-release rework.

notes: Stretch goal (requested 2026-11-11, experimental). Idea: WASAPI loopback capture feeding the visualizer's beat/level input; first find what the original visualizer reads (XMP / console music levels). 2026-11-12, built, untested (src/visualizer.cpp): how the original works: entering the Visualizer (sub_8207D250 state 2) calls XMPCaptureOutput (game wrapper sub_8215EFA0, XMP msg 0x7003D) with callback sub_82076F68; the console music player hands it 256 stereo frames (512 big-endian floats) at a time; the callback takes the level, an FFT and finds beats. Now: the wrapper is answered by the port, WASAPI loopback captures the PC's sound (process loopback leaving the game out, Windows 10 2004+; --visualizer_include_game for plain loopback), and the audio is handed to the callback on the game thread at the start of each game update (sub_8207D5F0). Then, untested: Visualizer Sensitivity (BBRR Settings, --visualizer_sensitivity 0.5/1/2/4): the music is level-matched (slow-falling peak brought to 0.8) and multiplied by the sensitivity before the game sees it. Tested: gain 1.5x vs 12x made no visible difference (the game finds beats relative to the music around them). Now, untested: sensitivity reshapes the dynamics instead: each 256-frame chunk scaled by (rms / 0.35 s average)^(e - 1), e = 0.35 / 1 / 1.6 / 2.2. 2026-11-12: sensitivity also scales the launcher's interval (game state 0x821A0578 +260) and level (+268) while the Visualizer runs, restored after; this gave a clear difference. acceptance: Modifiers option that blacks out the city behind the playfield during a song; arrows, fireworks and HUD unchanged
notes: Built 2026-11-11, untested: --no_background. SDK patch 0005 lets the port hide pixel shaders by the shader file they come from; the city is the only thing drawn with TextureModDiffuse.xpu, so its draws are skipped while game state is playing/failing. Street lights and smoke are point sprites and stay. The same SDK hook is a first step towards shader replacement by hash (R-408). 2026-11-11 first test: did nothing (log: city shader registered, never matched). The microcode in GPU memory has every word in the opposite byte order to the .xpu file and D3D renumbers a few registers when the shader is created (city: 10 of 12 words equal, hash 9567C79307ACC6F5). Matching is now 80% of words equal, in the right byte order; checked offline against the shader cache: only the city shader matches. Untested in game. 2026-11-11 (2): still no effect. The shader cache stores microcode in guest byte order, which is the file's byte order; the emulator's host dwords are those bytes read big-endian. The previous fix compared the wrong way round. Now: file words read big-endian, 80% of words equal (city 10 of 12, checked offline in the same terms). Untested. 2026-11-11 (3): the third build hid the arrows instead of the city: 9567C79307ACC6F5 is a generic textured shader from SimpleShaders.fxobj (12 of 12 words), used by the arrows; the city's shader matches none of the game's shader files. Approach changed: patch 0005 now hides draws by (vertex, pixel) shader hash pair, and the first time No Background is on in a song it logs every draw of two frames ('[bbrr] draw list ...') to identify the city's draws. Until those are filled in (kCityDraws in src/modifiers.cpp) the setting has no visible effect. 2026-11-11 (4): draw list read (two frames, ~1,500 draws each). Hidden now: sky 0C88/0AA0, backdrop BBFF/9567, city mesh passes C837/2B08 and 04F2/C9D2 with 6773/88B6, city details D1ED/238C; frames start with clears, so the space behind stays black. Arrows (436F/9567), fireworks (PointSprite 1DB9/C471, points 63B4/4B1E), glow passes and HUD untouched. List overridable with --no_background_draws. Untested. 2026-11-11 (5): city gone in play, sky still faintly visible; added sky dome 04F2/B36F and water quad B90D/FB9F to the list. Confirmed working in play 2026-11-11 (city, sky and water gone). Then: hidden from the Get Ready countdown on (screen scripts Ingame\GetReady / Hud start a song; LevelComplete, LevelBreakdown, GameOver, RetryMenu, HighScore, FireworkUnlocked, PostGame or Main\ end it), not only once the song plays; untested. 2026-11-12: renamed Background with Default / Off (Off hides the city); confirmed working.

title: Rocket Acceleration setting
acceptance: Modifiers > Rocket Acceleration: Default (the game's own movement) / Static (arrows move at one even speed)
notes: Built 2026-11-11, untested: --rocket_acceleration. sub_8206A328 eases arrows with (flown/flight)^1.5 across and ^1.05 upwards; a mid-asm hook at 0x8206A418 (where the eased and linear branches meet) sets both fractions to flown/flight when off. The game's own test byte 0x821A01C4 must not be written: it is the top byte of a value used elsewhere (0x8099FFF0 in the image) - writing it in the first attempt made acceleration flip unpredictably. Seen working 2026-11-11 (hard to tell by eye). The setting is read every frame, so it applies mid-song: arrows in the air move to their even-pace position at once (mostly a small sideways shift). 2026-11-12: reported reversed in play (On looked steady, Off looked accelerating - the original movement reads as steady on screen). Swapped: Off (default) = the game's own movement, On = the even pace along the path, which looks like speeding up. Then renamed at the user's request: values Default (game's own movement) and Static (even speed the whole way); cvar --rocket_acceleration false/true. Confirmed working; choices renamed Default / Static.

title: Horizontal Drift setting
acceptance: Modifiers > Horizontal Drift Default (original: arrows drift sideways towards their firework) / Off (straight up, in the screen column they first appear in)
notes: Built 2026-11-12, untested: --horizontal_drift. Mid-asm hook at 0x8206A4C8 (sub_8206A328, rocket's new position at r1+80 before it is stored): x is solved from the game's view matrix (game + 0x103B0..0x103E0, used by the arrow icons) so the rocket stays in its launch point's screen column; height and depth unchanged, so it meets the target line on time; trail, arrow and firework follow the rocket. Whether the matrix is applied as p x M or M x p is checked against the icons' clip coordinates (log line '[modifiers] arrow view matrix applied as ...'). Confirmed working 2026-11-12. 2026-11-12 rework: the screen column from the launch point drifted when the camera swung (Ode to Joy); solving world x for a fixed column then ran away (arrows flew about). Now: the rocket keeps its firework's x and z, then is slid along the camera's left-right direction (gradient of clip x) to the screen column it first appeared in, checked per frame. Choices Default / Off. Confirmed working on Ode to Joy 2026-11-12.

title: Autoplay
acceptance: Modifiers > Autoplay: every rocket hit at 0 ms (Perfect); a song in which it was on at any moment (countdown to end) saves no score locally or to leaderboards
notes: Built 2026-11-12, untested: src/autoplay.cpp. Presses go through the game's own controller read (sub_820E6E50, XamInputGetState wrapper): the due rocket's button is added for one read; the judging hook judges it at the rocket's time. Button per rocket byte +8: first guess 0=A 1=B 2=X 3=Y (the game's colour order Green, Red, Blue, Yellow), self-corrects when a press is not judged, kept in cache/autoplay_buttons.txt. Scores: leaderboard writes ignored for that song; results-screen profile save (GUI.save_needed) skipped for the rest of the run. Note: the game's save does not reach disk yet anyway (R-107). 2026-11-12 first test: no presses at all (no button table written). User confirmed arrow colour = button (green A, red B, blue X, yellow Y). Second build: no filter on button value or player byte (any value learns its own button, first guess value % 4 = A, B, X, Y), plus one-off log lines: the first rockets' bytes 0-11, and pad reads / rockets tracked / presses in the first 5 s of play. Second test: still no automatic hits; the user's own presses all read 0.00. Log: ~190 pad reads a second (more than one per frame: menus and gameplay both read), so a button held for one read was usually missed by the gameplay read; rocket byte 8 is 0/2/4/6 (byte 1 the matching bit). Third build: byte 8 / 2 -> A, B, X, Y (colour order), buttons held 35 ms with a 30 ms gap, only Autoplay's own presses judged at 0 ms, self-learning removed. Third build confirmed working 2026-11-12. Confirmed working 2026-11-12. 2026-11-12 (later), untested: playing along gave non-zero timings because the player's own press could judge a rocket before Autoplay's (not stale input); now the player's A/B/X/Y are removed from the controller read while the song clock moves (pause menu unaffected). Achievements blocked too: hook on XUserWriteAchievements (sub_820E7478, XGI message 0xB0008) sends a count of 0 when Autoplay was used in the song. 2026-11-12 (evening): Autoplay did not press anything when the song was played from the second controller: presses only ever went to controller slot 0. Now they go to the slot that plays (UIGlobals.primary_pad, reported by ui_scripts/Ingame/Hud.lua) and, in two-player modes, to each rocket's own player (rocket byte 11). Built, not run. Still to test: that a song played with Autoplay saves no leaderboard score. 2026-11-12 (evening, Leaderboards Test on): Autoplay from the second controller now presses (user-confirmed) and the score was not saved, but (1) a firework was unlocked and (2) the results screen ignored every button: when the game ends its Xbox Live session it only lets go of the controller once the profile save has started, and Autoplay skips that save (it would have waited 60 s). Fixes, built, not run: the judging function's 'is this firework unlocked already' question (sub_8207A6E0 called from 0x82066B14) is answered yes in an Autoplay song, so nothing unlocks; LevelBreakdown.lua marks the skipped save as started (GUI.started_save) so the screen carries on. Confirmed 2026-11-12: no unlock and the results screen carries on. The 'new high score' screen still appeared after an Autoplay song; ui_scripts/Ingame/LevelComplete.lua now clears UIGlobals.show_highscore_achieved in an Autoplay song (bbrr.autoplay.song). Not run.
